title: Mahdist State
capsule: The Mahdist State emerged in Sudan after Muhammad Ahmad declared himself the Mahdi in 1881, rallied the Ansar movement against Ottoman-Egyptian rule, and captured Khartoum in January 1885, killing Governor-General Charles Gordon. His successor Abdallahi ibn Muhammad (the Khalifa) governed from Omdurman under a rigorous interpretation of Islamic law, but persistent military overstretch, famine, and epidemic disease devastated the population. Anglo-Egyptian forces under Kitchener defeated the Mahdist army at the Battle of Omdurman on 2 September 1898, killing approximately 10,000 Ansar warriors, and the Khalifa himself was killed at the Battle of Umm Diwaykarat in November 1899, ending the state. Sudan then passed under Anglo-Egyptian Condominium rule, which lasted until 1956.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The state's territorial extent is well documented through British military survey records and contemporary accounts; boundary fluctuations during the 1880s–1890s campaigns are less precise.
